evidence: Deepseek: "At each step, pick a point with this x not using used y or z"; GLM: "all x's are distinct, all y's are distinct, all z's are distinct"
affordance_in_statement: Interference occurs if any two selected pockets share the same depth, the same latitude, or the same longitude.
secondary_shortcut_name: exactly-k implies one point per x
removal_suggestion: Extend the interference definition with an additional independently checked relation, rather than allowing conflicts to depend only on equality of x, y, or z.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: DFS fixes one selected pocket for every x and tracks only used y and z values.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Interference occurs if any two selected pockets share the same depth, the same latitude, or the same longitude.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the task as choosing k pockets with pairwise-distinct x, y, and z coordinates, then attempts a matching reduction.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Interference occurs if any two selected pockets share the same depth, the same latitude, or the same longitude.

common_affordance: The only incompatibilities are equality of the three individual coordinates; no additional relation between two pockets needs to be tracked.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its matching construction does not correctly enforce the full three-way compatibility condition, so a bipartite-style reduction can accept an invalid combination.
It uses an exponential backtracking/search approach and exceeds the time limit on dense or adversarial inputs.

recommended_edit: Change the interference sentence to: "Interference occurs if any two selected pockets share the same depth, latitude, or longitude, or if they have the same value of x+y+z." Add tests containing coordinate-disjoint pockets with equal x+y+z.
